accuracy.why: The three strings carry every fact of both sources and add none: the lead keeps the source's frame (from the storied Qaisariyah to the oasis gardens and farms), its three activities in order and its closing place name; «تاریخی» is the source's 'storied' / «العريقة», not a superlative. Two points off: the closing word «سوغاتیں» (round 1) is narrower than 'bounty' / «خيرات» — the land's good things become its specialties to take home and taste; and the title's «زرعی فارم» says 'agricultural' where the source says 'farms' (the approved nav.leisure pair, N5).

nativeness.why: The reader found the title clear and consistent across the page and the lead smooth up to its last clause; that clause («نعمتوں کا ذائقہ لیں», brochure-translated to him, item 3) is replaced by his own wording «الاحساء کی سوغاتیں چکھیں», which also ends the three-stage drift between «چکھیں», «ذائقہ چکھیں» and «ذائقہ لیں» on a concrete object that «چکھنا» takes naturally. Four points off: «سیاحتی رہنما» read first as a person (item 1, moderate; the same residue the b0-ui judge charged), kept so that the two sister indexes carry one eyebrow (N190); «تفریح گاہیں» slightly formal to him (item 2, minor; the native word the line chose over «پارک», P16); and the new clause is not yet read in place (the r1 blind read tests it).

compliance.why: «سوق القیصریہ» and «الاحساء» byte for byte their termbase keys; «نخلستان», «باغ», «فارم» (oblique «فارموں»), «تفریح گاہ» as entered; the title and eyebrow byte-identical to their approved tm.json pairs; Urdu letterforms only, «،» and «۔» only, the colon for the source's dash as in the approved list.lead; no Latin letter, no digit; honorific imperatives. «سوغات» is feminine (rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-saugaat, «اسم، مؤنث»), so «الاحساء کی سوغاتیں» agrees.

fit.why: The lead tells a traveller who knows nothing of Al-Ahsa what the page holds and what to do there, and as a search snippet it names the place and its best-known market (now one clause shorter). One point off: the eyebrow says nothing about this page to a reader who takes it for a person (item 1). The page's grouping, its missing hours and fees and the date-palm heading are SOURCE defects (logged below, no point taken).

structure.why: Exactly the pack's three ids in pack order, no placeholder, no bracket or final stop in the title or eyebrow, the lead closes with «۔» as its English closes with a stop. The JSON-LD name (list2.title + brand) is never seen by the blind reader: checked here — identical to the h1 and to nav.leisure, no Latin name inside it.

changes.before: الاحساء کی نعمتوں کا ذائقہ لیں۔
changes.why: Blind reader item 3 (minor): «نعمتوں کا ذائقہ لیں» reads as brochure language translated word for word; his wording taken as written. «چکھنا» now has a concrete object (the reason stage 2 objected to «نعمتیں چکھیں»), and neither «مزہ چکھنا» nor «ذائقہ چکھنا» (the 'suffer the consequences' idioms stage 4 found) is in it. «سوغات»: Rekhta «سَوْغات — اسم، مؤنث — gift or present, especially one brought from a far-off land» (HTTP 200, fetched by this stage), so «کی» agrees. Nothing enters: the verb is the source's 'taste' / «ذُق», the possessor its 'of Al-Ahsa'; cost on record under accuracy (specialties for 'bounty'). Unverified until the proof pass and the fresh blind read on r1.

calibration.question: list2.lead: the bare «نخلستان» for 'the oasis', or the oasis named («الاحساء کے نخلستان»), given that the lead is also the meta description?
candidates: A (in the text): the bare noun, as the source says
B: «… الاحساء کے نخلستان کے باغوں اور فارموں تک … یہاں کی …»
calibration.evidence: N47 binds a page that mentions the oasis and names it nowhere, and is expressly no rule about a summary read on its own. The rendered index names it («الاحساء کے نخلستان کے ماحول میں ایک باغ،», bird-garden card), and the lead itself closes on «الاحساء». The reader read the snippet and the lead (items 3, 4) and did not ask which oasis.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: A. An interface lead that says 'the oasis' as its source does keeps the bare «نخلستان» where the same sentence names Al-Ahsa; B moves the source's closing name and is not needed.
calibration.binds: list2.lead; any later interface lead of the same build.
calibration.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a lead with the bare «نخلستان» names «الاحساء» in the same sentence.

calibration.question: list2.lead: the closing clause for 'taste the bounty of Al-Ahsa' / «ذُق خيرات الأحساء».
candidates: A (stage 4): «الاحساء کی نعمتوں کا ذائقہ لیں»
B (stage 2): «الاحساء کی نعمتوں کا ذائقہ چکھیں»
D (blind reader, item 3): «الاحساء کی سوغاتیں چکھیں»
calibration.evidence: The reader read A in place and called it brochure language translated word for word; '«ذائقہ لیں» with «نعمتیں» is not how we would put it' (item 3, minor). B carries the 'suffer the consequences' idiom (Rekhta meaning-of-zaaiqa-chakhnaa); C gives «چکھنا» an abstract object (stage 2). D gives «چکھنا» a concrete object; «سَوْغات» is a feminine noun, 'gift, especially one brought from a far-off land' (rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-saugaat, HTTP 200, fetched by stage 7).
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: D, provisional until the r1 proof pass and fresh blind read: «… اور الاحساء کی سوغاتیں چکھیں۔». Cost on record: 'specialties' is narrower than 'bounty'. If the r1 reader stops at it, A is the fallback; B is withdrawn (idiom).
calibration.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: neither «مزہ چکھ» nor «ذائقہ چکھ» in the line's text for a pleasant tasting.

calibration.question: list2.lead: «سوق القیصریہ» bare (P3c-labels: the string is a meta description) or with the running-text form «نامی بازار» (P3c point 2)?
candidates: A (in the text): the name bare, byte for byte its key
B: «تاریخی سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار سے لے کر …»
calibration.evidence: The reader named «سوق القیصریہ» in the lead without a pause (item 4); his item 29 finds the mix of «سوق» names and translated «بازار» names understandable. The h1 above opens with «بازار». cat.market.d writes the name bare.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: A. A string that is both a lead and a meta description follows P3c-labels: the name stands bare; the plain generic stands in the neighbouring line (the h1).
calibration.binds: list2.lead; every interface string that doubles as a meta description.
calibration.guard: Stage checker, as today: no bracket and no Urdu generic next to a name that carries its Arabic generic in such a string.

calibration.question: list2.lead: «فارموں» bare in running text, or «زرعی فارموں» (N5's label form)?
candidates: A (in the text): «نخلستان کے باغوں اور فارموں تک»
B: «… باغوں اور زرعی فارموں تک»
calibration.evidence: The reader quoted «نخلستان کے باغوں اور فارموں» (item 4) and read it without a remark; he did not read 'forms'.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: A. N5's qualifier is a label rule; in running text beside «باغوں» the bare oblique «فارموں» stands, as on zaki-alsalem-farm.
calibration.guard: For the proofreader: «زرعی» before «فارم» in a label or heading standing alone; not required in running text.

calibration.question: list2.eyebrow: keep «سیاحتی رہنما» (the approved list.eyebrow, live on the sister attractions index) although the reader first read it as a person?
candidates: A (in the text): «سیاحتی رہنما», identical to list.eyebrow
C: a new native wording here only
calibration.evidence: Reader item 1 (moderate): first read as a tour guide, understood only at the footer «یہ ویب سائٹ ایک آزاد سیاحتی رہنما ہے». The b0-ui judge charged the same personal reading under nativeness with no wording offered. B uses the banned loan «گائیڈ». C would give the two sister indexes different eyebrows for the same English ('Visit guide'), which ru/de/zh do not do, and would break the approved tm.json pair.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: A. The two sister eyebrows stay one string; the cost is charged under nativeness and fit. A rewording, if ever taken, moves list.eyebrow and list2.eyebrow (and their tm.json pairs) together in one interface batch and is read in place; never «گائیڈ».
calibration.binds: list.eyebrow, list2.eyebrow and every later index eyebrow of the same English.
calibration.guard: For the proofreader: an index eyebrow whose English is 'Visit guide' is byte-identical to list.eyebrow; «گائیڈ» is a banned loan (stage checker).
